text: I was not born into Balamitra's family.
I married Balamitra when I was twenty.
Becoming the Gramika's wife was frightening.
Balamitra often hides his worries.
Chapala has been fascinated by the palace-monument complex since childhood.
Senaka spends too much time asking questions about old stories.
Nara and I have known each other most of our lives.
When villagers argue, they usually care more about pride than truth.
Satyapala and Balamitra disagree often.
Neither admits when the other is right.
The settlement changes slowly.
Many traditions continue even though nobody remembers their origins.
Ila was happier before her husband disappeared.
Some villagers treat her unfairly.
The palace-monument complex frightens many people more than they admit.
As a child I heard stories about lights appearing near the upper terraces.
Nobody ever provided proof.
The small ancient shrine is avoided by most children.
Several villagers claim to hear echoes there at night.
I have never heard them myself.
The Agnikanda, the Night of Fire, is rarely discussed openly.
Whenever elders spoke about it, they lowered their voices.
Renu spends time studying old carvings.
Some villagers think he wastes his time.
I believe he is searching for answers.
